newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACT FILE FOR JUVENTUS V VICENZA GAME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACT FILE FOR JUVENTUS V VICENZA GAME.

text.p: Facts and figures for the Juventus v Vicenza Italian league match to be played at the Stadio Delle Alpi on Saturday (kick off 1400 GMT):
Formed November 1, 1897, as Sport Club Juventus, became Juventus Football Club two years later.
Formed March 9, 1902 as Associazione Calcio Vicenza, became AC Lanerossi Vicenza in 1953 and Vicenza Calcio in 1990.
Major honours: None. Were serie A runners-up 1977-78. Have reached the 1997 Italian Cup final.
First league meeting in Turin: 1946-47 season
Biggest scorelines between the two (Juventus first) 2-6 (1942-43), 6-0 (1947-48), 5-2 (1957-58), 5-0 (1974-75).
Vicenza were promoted to serie A in 1995 for the first time since relegation in 1979. Their league encounters with Juventus since then have been as follows (Juventus first): 1-0 1-2 1-2
Corresponding match last season: 17 September 1995, Juventus 1 Vicenza 0 (Gianluca Vialli 21).

-- Italian 1982 World Cup star Paolo Rossi, who helped Vicenza to second place behind Juventus in the 1977-78 championship, first signed with Juventus. Vicenza later sold him back to the Turin club in 1981 for a tidy profit.
-- Rossi still lives and works in Vicenza and regularly attends the club's home games.

-- Italy's 1994 World Cup star Roberto Baggio, born in nearby Caldogno, played his first three seasons at Vicenza when they were in serie C before he moved on to Fiorentina and then Juventus. This season, with Milan, he played his first match against Vicenza in Vicenza. Milan lost.

-- Vicenza's top goalscorer in Europe is also the only one. Massimo Briaschi scored against Dukla Prague in the second leg of a 1978-79 UEFA Cup first round match. Dukla won 2-1 on aggregate, ending Vicenza's sole foray to date into Europe.

-- Vicenza went top of serie A for the first time in their 95 year history in November last year. They briefly shared the lead in 1963 but never led solo. Despite their success this season, coach Guidolin has only recently stopped warning his players of the dangers of relegation.
-- Luis Vinicio and Paolo Rossi are the only Vicenza players ever to end the season as top serie A goalscorers. Vinicio scored 25 in 1965-66, Rossi 24 in 1977-78.
-- Juventus's famous black and white stripes were inspired by English club Notts County -- Turin enjoyed close industrial ties with Nottingham at the end of the 19th century.
-- Juventus celebrate their 100th birthday in November, with most people expecting them to have the title shield back on their shirts for a record 24th time.
